sampling_model.design: Observational two-cohort four-wave panel \(O=(D,X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3)\), with adoption at date \(3\), a finite active state space of size \(m\), a common absorbing exit, fixed known \(2\leq J\leq m\), and possible date-\(1\) absorption in the headline class.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent and identically distributed complete four-wave panels on the \(N_m=2\sum_{r=0}^{4}m^r\)-cell absorption-legal support; \(N_2=62\). A recorded fifth wave is unnecessary and may be marginalized out.
sampling_model.treatment: Cohort membership fixes the realized path; no anticipation holds through date \(2\), and units absorbed by date \(1\) have identical absorbed potential continuations through the first post-treatment date.
sampling_model.overlap: Both cohorts have positive probability. Positive active masses \(\alpha_j^d\) and hence positive full masses \(\pi_j^d\) follow from anchor-star nonsingularity rather than a separate type-overlap assumption.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is fitted. Empirical frequencies on the fixed four-wave \(N_m\)-cell support feed the guarded analytic anchor-star recovery map.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 14 reconstructs latent transition components under its stated full-rank and positive-transition conditions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Four anchor slices determine the spectral basis, and the observable anchor-star slices transport recovery to all active states at the excluded common-absorbing boundary.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 reconstructs Markov-mixture components under its time-homogeneous and component-rank conditions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The known-J theorem uses selected active minors and stochastic normalization without time homogeneity and does not claim to subsume that reconstruction theorem.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper studies homogeneous Markov-mixture reconstruction under its state-count and nondegeneracy restrictions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present result is causal, time-varying, permits an absorbing boundary, and treats fixed known J no larger than the active-state count.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper develops aggregate duration difference-in-differences under absorption-oriented restrictions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present theorem reconstructs latent-type multi-state contributions and isolates the initial-absorber frontier for conditional effects.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper estimates latent conditional moments by simultaneous diagonalization and derives regular asymptotics for estimated weights.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The analytic-gradient theorem differentiates the known-J anchor-star row-sum, pseudoinverse, and full-row transport map on the absorption-legal support.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Gaussian comparison and anti-concentration permit arbitrary correlation when marginal variances are positive.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The uniform-band theorem adds the buffered empirical guard and quantile continuity at singular correlation limits for this fixed-dimensional recovery map.

body.tldr: For fixed known \(2\leq J\leq m\), four observed waves \(X_0,\ldots,X_3\) suffice. Four anchor slices determine the spectral basis, and \(2m-1\) fixed selected anchor-star minors transport it to every active state despite a common absorbing boundary. Projectors, stochastic row sums, a full-row-rank pseudoinverse, and full-predecessor-row transport recover active component sublaws, type contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate first-post ATT on the broad class; no date-\(1\) absorption upgrades these to full type shares and full conditional type effects. The resulting \(N_m=2\sum_{r=0}^{4}m^r\)-cell functional has an explicit saturated multinomial canonical gradient and guarded uniform Gaussian-multiplier bands under singular correlation. Restricted-model efficiency remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published short-panel Markov-mixture reconstruction and the closest transition-independence theorem impose rank, positivity, homogeneity, emission, or state-count conditions that do not deliver four-wave causal recovery at a common absorbing boundary. They also do not characterize the initial-absorber frontier, where full latent shares and conditional type effects can fail although active contributions and the aggregate remain identified.
project_justification.niche: For fixed known \(J\leq m\), fixed ex ante row and column selections, and an observable anchor star of \(2m-1\) nonsingular selected minors, four anchor slices identify a common spectral basis while the remaining star slices transport it across active states. Stochastic normalization handles exit, and absorption plus no anticipation makes date-\(1\) absorbers a zero-effect component.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives the explicit four-wave known-\(J\) projector, row-sum, pseudoinverse, and full-row transport map; proves the active-versus-full target frontier and a generic initial-absorber allocation counterexample; verifies an exact rational \(J=m=2\) witness; and derives the analytic saturated gradient plus guarded uniform multiplier bands.

body.related_work: Ahn and Kasahara (2026), Proposition 14 and Appendix A.4, provide the closest inverse-cancellation architecture, but their stated full-rank and positive-transition conditions exclude the common absorbing boundary; the present four-wave result is an excluded-boundary extension, not an application of their theorem. Higgins and Jochmans (2023) and Gupta, Kumar, and Vassilvitskii (2016) reconstruct Markov mixtures under their own homogeneity, component-rank, state-count, and nondegeneracy regimes; their scaling and label ideas are prior art, whereas the present theorem is causal, time-varying, and uses fixed known \(J\leq m\) selected anchor-star minors. Restricted hidden-Markov reconstruction results impose emission or other structural restrictions and do not prove the potential-path contribution identity here. Deaner and Ku (2026) study aggregate duration difference-in-differences rather than latent-type multi-state reconstruction. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2017) motivate differentiating diagonalization estimators, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, 2015) are neighboring Gaussian-bootstrap and anti-concentration references. Rao and Risch (2026) are an interpretation consumer only: this paper does not claim their data satisfy the latent Markov, rank, support, or iid conditions. Restricted-model efficiency is left as an explicit open question.
body.interpretation:
The four-wave result separates the full type share \(\pi_j^d\), active share \(\alpha_j^d\), unnormalized contribution \(
u_j\), and at-risk effect \(\eta_j\). The \(2m-1\) anchor-star slices identify \(\alpha_j^d\), \(
u_j\), and \(\eta_j=
u_j/\alpha_j^1\), with positivity derived from nonsingularity. They cannot allocate already-absorbed zero-effect mass across latent labels, so full shares and full conditional effects need not be identified. If date-\(1\) absorption is absent, \(\pi_j^d=\alpha_j^d\) and \(	au_j=\eta_j\). The exact \(H_1,H_2,Q_1,Q_2,V_1,V_2\) witness verifies the cycle operator, type effects, and aggregate rationally, while its all-exit reallocation exhibits the frontier. Rao and Risch's incumbent-firm setting motivates this decomposition but is not reanalyzed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance \(\Sigma(p)\) is the canonical-gradient bound for the declared off-model continuation \(\Phi\) in the saturated four-wave finite-multinomial support-stratum model. The paper does not parameterize the smaller restricted Markov observed-law image, certify its score Jacobian on constant-rank strata, or claim its efficiency bound or an attaining estimator. The exact multiplier quantile is the mathematical object; a fixed Monte Carlo draw count requires separate approximation analysis. Weak eigengaps, changing selected-minor rank, unknown \(J\), adaptive anchor selection, clustered sampling, and approximate common kernels remain outside the result.
body.honest_scope: The paper proves a sufficient constructive frontier for fixed finite \(m\), known \(2\leq J\leq m\), four observed waves, fixed ex ante selected sets and anchor pairs, \(2m-1\) observable anchor-star nonsingularity conditions, distinct common cycle signatures, cohort overlap, type-conditional first-order Markov potential paths through date \(3\), no anticipation, absorption, and common untreated date-\(2\) and first-post kernels. It derives rather than assumes type positivity. The exact rational witness establishes nonvacuity and the initial-absorber pair establishes the stated obstruction. The paper does not identify unknown type count, choose minors adaptively, cover weak or complex spectra, justify dependent-panel inference, or solve restricted-model efficiency. Full conditional type effects require no date-\(1\) absorption; the broad class identifies active sublaws, contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate.
